strategy_definition.summary: Using intermarket analysis (Bonds and Dollar) to establish a directional bias, then comparing correlated assets (like EU vs GU or ES vs NQ) to select the relatively stronger pair for longs or weaker pair for shorts.

timeframes.notes: Uses higher timeframe to establish the overarching draw on liquidity and relative strength, before dropping to lower timeframes for execution.

other: Intermarket synchronization (Bonds and Dollar moving inversely)

glossary.DECOUPLED: When two correlated assets are not moving as they should (e.g., Dollar and Bonds both going higher), indicating a low-probability 'Seek and Destroy' condition.
glossary.FILTERING PROCESS: The sequence of analyzing Bonds -> Dollar -> Asset Class -> Correlated Pairs to find the absolute highest probability instrument to trade.
glossary.RELATIVE STRENGTH: When comparing two correlated pairs, the one that makes a bigger explosive move or fails to sweep a structural point that the other pair swept.

custom_signals.name: decoupled_market
custom_signals.plain_definition: 30-year Treasury Bonds and the US Dollar moving in the same directional trend or consolidating heavily, rather than being inversely correlated.

custom_signals.name: relatively_stronger_pair
custom_signals.plain_definition: Between two correlated assets (e.g., EU and GU), the one that shows a more explosive move in the bias direction or fails to break a swing low when the other does.

sequence: Analyze the 30-year Treasury Bond (ZB) for a higher timeframe direction.
Analyze the US Dollar; ensure it is moving inversely to the Bonds. If they are moving together (decoupled), expect low probability or consolidation.
Establish a clear draw on liquidity on the Dollar to form a directional bias for Forex or Indices.
Compare correlated assets (e.g., EURUSD vs GBPUSD, or ES vs NQ vs YM).
If looking for buys (Dollar expected to drop), select the relatively stronger pair.
If looking for sells (Dollar expected to rise), select the relatively weaker pair.
Wait for the chosen pair to reach a discount/premium array and look for an entry confirmation (like SMT divergence).

invalidation.text: If Bonds and the Dollar are decoupled, the market indicates a 50/50 bias and low probability Seek and Destroy conditions.

filters.text: If the bonds have been consolidating heavily, take them less into account and rely more directly on the Dollar.
Beginners should avoid this filtering process and just focus on mastering one single pair to build patience.

entry_rule.text: Wait for price to reach a discount/premium array on the chosen pair, then use lower timeframe confirmation (like SMT, breaker, or swing failure) as taught in previous episodes.
entry_rule.quote: when we are waiting for confirmation we look for smt so whether the breaker or the swing failure happens

target_rule.text: Target the opposing draw on liquidity established on the higher timeframe.
target_rule.quote: this already tells me a lot of what my drone quality will likely be on EU then we have this liquidity pool right there

stop_rule.text: Not explicitly covered in this pair-selection video.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Analyzes the US Dollar chart to establish a bearish bias, aiming for a lower liquidity pool after mitigating a Daily FVG.
Switches to EURUSD (EU) to show harmony with the Dollar, establishing the draw on liquidity upwards.
Compares EU directly with GBPUSD (GU). GU makes a bigger, more explosive upward move and fails to take a high that EU might have, showing SMT and Relative Strength.
Concludes that because GU is relatively stronger, it is the highest probability pair to look for buys in a discount array.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: He uses the divergence between EU and GU to prove that you shouldn't just pick any pair going against the Dollar. You must pick the one showing relative strength for longs to maximize probability and payout.
